section.content: Example embodiments of the present disclosure relate to a technical solution for improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) localization. In one aspect, a terminal device receives, from a network device, a channel measurement for the terminal device, and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) pattern models stored in the terminal device. The terminal device sends the channel measurement and the first information to the network device. The terminal device receives second information from the network device regarding a target TRP pattern model for positioning among the plurality of TRP pattern models. In this way, a trade-off between model performance, model complexity, and computational complexity may be achieved. Furthermore, an appropriate TRP mode model for positioning at the current wireless environment of the terminal device may be determined, thereby improving AI/ML positioning accuracy.

本公开的示例实施例涉及用于改进人工智能（AI）或机器学习（ML）定位的技术方案。在一个方面，一种终端设备从网络设备接收针对终端设备的信道测量、以及关于存储在终端设备中的多个传输接收点（TRP）模式模型的第一信息的请求。终端设备向网络设备发送信道测量和第一信息。终端设备从网络设备接收关于多个TRP模式模型中用于定位的目标TRP模式模型的第二信息。以这种方式，可以实现模型性能、模型复杂性和计算复杂性之间的权衡。此外，可以确定用于终端设备的当前无线环境处的定位的适当TRP模式模型，从而提高AI/ML定位精度。

Artificial intelligence or machine learning positioningTechnical Field

Various example embodiments relate to the field of communications, and in particular, to apparatus, methods, devices, and computer-readable storage media for improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) positioning accuracy.

Background

A communication network may be considered a facility that enables communication between two or more communication devices or that provides a communication device with access to a data network. A mobile or wireless communication network is one example of a communication network. The communication device may be provided with a service by an application server. Such communication networks operate according to standards such as those provided by 3GPP (third generation partnership project) or ETSI (european telecommunications standards institute). An example of a standard is the so-called 5G (fifth generation) standard provided by 3 GPP.

From a standardization perspective, 3GPP release 18 has approved research to enhance the benefits of the air interface through recent advances in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML), and AI/ML positioning accuracy enhancement is considered one of the most representative use cases. According to the protocols, 3GPP agrees to study the necessity, feasibility and potential impact on specifications of methods for assessing or monitoring the applicability and expected performance of inactive models or functions.

Disclosure of Invention

In general, example embodiments of the present disclosure provide a technical solution for improving the model environment adaptability of AI/ML positioning, in particular for monitoring a Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode model.

In a first aspect, a terminal device is provided. The terminal device may include at least one processor and at least one memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the terminal device to at least receive a channel measurement for the terminal device from a network device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) pattern models stored in the terminal device, send the channel measurement and the first information to the network device, and receive second information regarding a target TRP pattern model for positioning from among the plurality of TRP pattern models from the network device.

In a second aspect, a network device is provided. The network device may include at least one processor and at least one memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the network device to at least transmit a request to a terminal device for channel measurements for the terminal device and first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device, receive the channel measurements and the first information from the terminal device, determine second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning among the plurality of TRP mode models based on the channel measurements and the first information, and transmit the second information to the terminal device.

In a third aspect, a method is provided. The method may include receiving, at a terminal device, a channel measurement for the terminal device from a network device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device, transmitting, by the terminal device, the channel measurement and the first information to the network device, and receiving, by the terminal device, second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning from among the plurality of TRP mode models from the network device.

In a fourth aspect, a method is provided. The method may include transmitting, by a network device, channel measurements for the terminal device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device to the terminal device, receiving, by the network device, the channel measurements and the first information from the terminal device, determining, by the network device, second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning among the plurality of TRP mode models based on the channel measurements and the first information, and transmitting, by the network device, the second information to the terminal device.

In a fifth aspect, an apparatus is provided. The apparatus may include means for receiving a channel measurement for a terminal device from a network device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device, means for transmitting the channel measurement and the first information to the network device, and means for receiving second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning from among the plurality of TRP mode models from the network device.

In a sixth aspect, an apparatus is provided. The apparatus may include means for transmitting a channel measurement for a terminal device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device to the terminal device, means for receiving the channel measurement and the first information from the terminal device, means for determining second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning among the plurality of TRP mode models based on the channel measurement and the first information, and means for transmitting the second information to the terminal device.

In a seventh aspect, there is provided a non-transitory computer readable medium comprising program instructions which, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to perform at least the method according to any one of the third and fourth aspects.

In an eighth aspect, there is provided a computer program comprising instructions which, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to perform at least the method according to any one of the third and fourth aspects.

In a ninth aspect, a terminal device is provided. The terminal device may include first transmit circuitry configured to receive a channel measurement for the terminal device from a network device and a request for first information about a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) pattern models stored in the terminal device, second transmit circuitry configured to transmit the channel measurement and the first information to the network device, and receive circuitry configured to receive second information about a target TRP pattern model for positioning from the plurality of TRP pattern models from the network device.

In a tenth aspect, a network device is provided. The network device may include first transmit circuitry configured to transmit a channel measurement for the terminal device and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device to the terminal device, receive circuitry configured to receive the channel measurement and the first information from the terminal device, determine circuitry configured to determine second information regarding a target TRP mode model for positioning among the plurality of TRP mode models based on the channel measurement and the first information, and second transmit circuitry configured to transmit the second information to the terminal device.

It should be understood that the summary is not intended to identify key or essential features of the embodiments of the disclosure, nor is it intended to be used to limit the scope of the disclosure. Other features of the present disclosure will become apparent from the following description.

With the development of communication technology, 3GPP began to support AI/ML positioning over the latest RAN population conferences with the goals of (1) positioning accuracy enhancement for UE-based positioning using a UE-side model, and direct AI/ML positioning, might be required, (2) specifying the necessary measurements and signaling mechanism(s) to facilitate location accuracy enhancement case-specific lifecycle management (LCM) operations, (3) it required a method to ensure consistency between training and reasoning with respect to network device-side additional conditions (if identified) for reasoning at the UE for relevant positioning.

According to the protocols, 3GPP agrees to study the necessity, feasibility and potential impact on specifications of methods for assessing or monitoring the applicability and expected performance of inactive models or functions. In addition, 3GPP also agrees to study the monitoring method to ensure consistency between training and reasoning. For example, for reasoning on the UE-side model, consistency between training and reasoning on NW-side additional conditions (if identified) needs to be ensured. This may be a potential method for ensuring consistency between training and reasoning by monitoring the performance of the UE-side candidate models or functions (by the UE and/or NW) to select the model or function. Thus, for model/function based LCM, there must be a monitoring mechanism to evaluate the adaptability of the model or function, and the mechanism needs to be specified explicitly.

In view of the foregoing, some embodiments of the present disclosure propose a solution for improving AI/ML positioning accuracy, e.g., for monitoring model environment adaptation of a Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode model. In some example embodiments of the present disclosure, a terminal device receives, from a network device, a channel measurement for the terminal device, and a request for first information regarding a plurality of Transmission Reception Point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device. The terminal device sends the channel measurement and the first information to the network device. The terminal device receives second information from the network device regarding a target TRP pattern model for positioning among the plurality of TRP pattern models. In this way, an appropriate TRP mode model for positioning at the current wireless environment of the terminal device can be determined, thereby improving AI/ML positioning accuracy, in particular monitoring the model environment adaptability of the TRP mode model.

Fig. 1A illustrates an example network environment 100 in which example embodiments of the present disclosure may be implemented. The environment 100, which may be part of a communication network, includes terminal devices and network devices. As shown in fig. 1A, communication network 100 may include a terminal device 110. The communication network 100 may further include a network device 120, a network device 130 (hereinafter may also be referred to as TRP or site), and a network device 140 (hereinafter may also be referred to as network device including a Location Management Function (LMF)). In DL positioning, the network device or TRP 120 and TRP 130 may send Positioning Reference Signals (PRSs) to the terminal device 110, and the network device 140 may request the terminal device 110 to collect PRS samples for each selected TRP 120 or TRP 130.

It should be understood that the number of network devices and terminal devices is for illustration purposes only and is not meant to be limiting in any way. System 100 may include any suitable number of network devices and/or terminal devices suitable for implementing embodiments of the present disclosure. Although not shown, it is to be appreciated that one or more terminal devices can reside within the environment 100.

Further, the communications may utilize any suitable wireless communication technology including, but not limited to, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), time Division Multiplexing (TDM), frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM), code Division Multiplexing (CDM), bluetooth, zigBee, and Machine Type Communications (MTC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), large-scale machine type communications (mMTC), ultra-reliable low-delay communications (URLLC), carrier Aggregation (CA), dual Connectivity (DC), and new radio unlicensed (NR-U) technologies.

It should be understood that the number of devices and their connection relationships and types shown in fig. 1A are for illustrative purposes only and are not meant to be limiting in any way. As described above, in order to investigate the necessity, feasibility and potential impact on specifications of methods for assessing or monitoring the applicability and expected performance of inactive models or functions, 3GPP has agreed to investigate monitoring methods to ensure consistency between training and reasoning. For example, for reasoning on the UE-side model, consistency between training and reasoning on NW-side additional conditions (if identified) needs to be ensured. This may be a potential method for ensuring consistency between training and reasoning by monitoring the performance of the UE-side candidate models or functions (by the UE and/or NW) to select the model or function. Thus, for model or function based LCM, there must be a monitoring mechanism to evaluate the adaptability of the model or function and the mechanism needs to be specified explicitly.

Multiple TRP AI/ML localization was also assessed. For the evaluation of AI/ML-based localization, the study of model inputs due to the different numbers of TRPs includes two approaches. The supporters of each approach analyze for model performance, signaling overhead (including training data collection and model reasoning), model complexity, and computational complexity. For method 1, the model input size remains unchanged, ntrp=18. When N ' TRP < NTRP, the remaining (NTRP-N ' TRP) TRP does not provide a measure to the model input, i.e. the measure is set to 0, so that the (NTRP-N ' TRP) TRP does not affect the model output. For sub-method 1-A, the set of TRPs providing the measurement (N' TRPs) is fixed. However, for another sub-method 1-B, the set of TRPs (N' TRP) providing the measurement may be dynamically changed. The number of TRPs (N' TRPs) that provide a measurement for model inputs may vary.

For method 2, the TRP dimension of the model input is equal to the number of TRPs (N' TRPs) that are provided as model inputs for measurement. When N 'TRP < NTRP, the remaining (NTRP-N' TRP) TRPs are ignored by the given model. The set of TRP (N' TRP) providing the measurement is fixed for a given AI/ML model. For sub-method 2-A, the set of active TRPs (N' TRPs) providing the measurement is fixed. For sub-method 1-A and sub-method 2-A, one model can be provided to cover the entire assessment area, which is equivalent to deploying N 'TRPs in the assessment area for localization while ignoring the potential inferences of the remaining (18-N' TRPs). For sub-method 2-B, the set of active TRP (N' TRP) providing the measurement may be dynamically varied. For sub-method 2-B, a model was developed to handle the various modes of active TRP.

Thus, to facilitate AI/ML location enhancement in a multi-TRP scenario, it becomes critical to specify the necessary signaling mechanisms and implementation operations that favor LCM, which is specific to the identified use case. According to the 3GPP protocol, multi-TRP evaluations have been performed. Based on the evaluation results made by 8 sources, the method supporting dynamic TRP mode can achieve horizontal positioning accuracy E dynamic=(0.80~2.15)Efixed (meters) for TRP reduction of direct AI/ML positioning, where E dynamic is horizontal positioning accuracy achieved by dynamic TRP mode and E fixed is horizontal positioning accuracy achieved by fixed TRP mode.

For TRP reduction with AI/ML assisted localization of multi-TRP constructs, the method supporting dynamic TRP mode can achieve horizontal localization accuracy E dynamic=(1.03~1.74)Efixed (meters) based on the evaluation results from 2 sources, with other design parameters remaining unchanged. Here, E dynamic (meters) is the horizontal positioning accuracy of the method supporting the dynamic TRP mode (i.e., sub-methods 1-B and 2-B) at cdf=90%, and E fixed (meters) is the horizontal positioning accuracy of the method supporting the fixed TRP mode (i.e., sub-methods 1-a and 2-a) at cdf=90%.

Thus, according to the above summary, e.g., E dynamic=(0.80~2.15)Efixed (meters) or E dynamic=(1.03~1.74) Efixed (meters), models with fixed TRP patterns (i.e., sub-methods 1-a and 2-a) show better positioning accuracy in most cases. However, LCM signaling deployed for this fixed TRP mode model remains lacking.

Hereinafter, the deployment of an evaluation region for the entire region of the fixed TRP mode will be described with reference to fig. 1B. As shown in fig. 1B, the evaluation region is divided into three non-overlapping regions, e.g., region a, region B, and region C, and three fixed TRP pattern models may be trained for these regions.

To evaluate model suitability, a specific fixed TRP pattern model is trained for region a using the fixed TRP pattern, and then its localization performance is evaluated using other TRP patterns and test regions. The evaluation results are shown in Table 1.

TABLE 1 positioning accuracy of fixed TRP pattern models in different regions (such as region A, region B, and region C) and at different TRP patterns (e.g., different TRPs)

As shown in table 1, the first row is the baseline for comparison, and as shown in the first row, region a is trained by TRP 0,1, 2, 3. As shown in the second and third rows, it can be observed that positioning accuracy may deteriorate if the TRP pattern model is fixed in region a and tested with other TRP patterns (e.g., TRP 0,1, 2, 4 in the second row, and TRP 0, 2, 3, 5 in the third row) instead of the training TRP pattern (e.g., TRP 0,1, 2, 3). It can be seen that the 13.16 meter and 25.75 meter accuracy is lower than the 7.34 meter accuracy.

On the other hand, if the fixed TRP pattern model is tested with the training TRP pattern (e.g., TRP 0,1, 2, 3) in other areas, such as area B of the fourth row and area C of the fifth row, instead of the training area (e.g., area a), its performance will also deteriorate. It can be seen that 43.09 meters and 99.93 meters are less accurate than 7.34 meters. Thus, it can be concluded that for a fixed TRP mode model, that the model must be deployed in its same training region (e.g., region a) and the same TRP training mode (e.g., TRP 0,1, 2, 3) is used.

However, in actual deployment, when the UE has a plurality of fixed TRP mode models for the entire region, the UE lacks information of TRP deployment, and thus it is difficult for the UE to evaluate or evaluate which fixed TRP mode model is suitable for the current environment. In contrast, the Location Management Function (LMF) has TRP deployment knowledge and wireless channel information of the entire region, and the LMF can assist the UE in monitoring the model applicability. New signaling needs to be provided between the LMF and the UE to improve AI/ML positioning accuracy by ensuring consistency between training and reasoning about NW-side additional conditions.

Hereinafter, an example signal process 200 for monitoring environmental suitability of a TRP pattern model will be described with reference to fig. 2. For discussion purposes, the process 200 may be described with reference to FIG. 1A. As shown in fig. 1A, process 200 may involve terminal device 110 and network device 140. It should be appreciated that although the process 200 is described in the communication environment 100 of fig. 1A, the process is equally applicable to other communication scenarios with similar problems.

As shown in fig. 2, in process 200, a network device 140 (e.g., LMF) sends (205) to a terminal device 110 (e.g., UE) a request 201 for channel measurements for the terminal device 110 and first information about a plurality of transmission-reception point (TRP) mode models stored in the terminal device 110. Terminal device 110 receives (210) request 201 and then sends (215) the requested information 202 to network device 140, which information includes channel measurements and information about TRP mode models. The network device 140 receives (220) the requested information 202.

In some embodiments, the TRP mode model is a fixed TRP mode model, meaning that the set of TRPs providing the measurement (N 'TRP) is fixed or the set of active TRPs providing the measurement (N' TRP) is fixed. Terminal device 110 may store several TRP mode models for positioning and the TRP mode models have been trained by network device 140 (such as an LMF). For example, each pattern model is trained for each region, and TRP patterns for use in a plurality of TRP patterns may not overlap each other, and regions divided for training may not overlap each other.

In some embodiments, the channel measurements of the terminal device 110 and the first information about the plurality of TRP mode models stored in the terminal device 110 are necessary information for monitoring the adaptability between the models and the wireless environment. In some embodiments, the necessary information includes an input TRP index for each pre-stored model, and a received channel measurement for the terminal device. In some embodiments, the input TRP index for each pre-stored model is a TRP index for a training model. In some embodiments, the first information about the plurality of TRP mode models includes or is related to network side add-on conditions.

In some embodiments, the received channel measurements may be power information about the channel measurements, such as Reference Signal Receive Path Power (RSRPP), delay information about the channel measurements, such as delay Profile (PD), channel Impulse Response (CIR), power Delay Profile (PDP), or any combination thereof. For DP information, delay profiles mainly focus on signal profiles of different delay times, while PDP focuses on signal power profiles of different delay times. DP provides information on the distribution of signal arrival times, while PDP provides variation of signal power with delay time.

In some embodiments, the terminal device 110 may also send a request for monitoring the adaptability between the current TRP mode model and the wireless environment of the terminal device, and upon receiving the request for monitoring, the network device 140 may send a request 201 to the terminal device 110 for channel measurements and first information of the terminal device.

After receiving the channel measurement and the first information of the terminal device, the network device 140 may determine (225) second information 203 about a target TRP mode model for positioning among the plurality of TRP mode models based on the channel measurement and the first information of the terminal device. It should be understood that "based on" means "based at least in part on". In some embodiments, the network device 140 determines the second information based on the channel measurements of the terminal device, the first information, and a data set pre-stored in the network device or downloaded from a data center. In some embodiments, the data set pre-stored in the network device or downloaded from the data center may include channel measurements and location coordinates of all pre-stored TRPs for a particular entire region. In some embodiments, the target TRP mode model is the most appropriate positioning model of terminal device 110 in the current environment. Then, the network device 140 transmits (230) second information 203 about the target TRP mode model to the terminal device 110, and the terminal device 110 receives (235) the second information 203.

In some embodiments, network device 140 may determine whether terminal device 110 needs to switch the current model based on the second information and then send an indication of the target mode (e.g., the TRP mode of the target TRP mode model) to terminal device 110 along with the second information. If the target model is different from the model currently used by terminal device 110, indicating that the model used by terminal device 110 is not suitable for its current environment, network device 140 may determine that terminal device 110 needs to switch to the target model, and network device 140 may send an indication of the switch and the TRP mode of the target model to terminal device 110.

In some embodiments, upon receiving the information about the target TRP mode model, the terminal device 110 may determine whether the target TRP mode model is the same as the current model, and if so, the terminal device 110 may not switch the current model, and if not, the terminal device 110 may switch from the current model to the target model.

In process 200, a method and associated signaling for monitoring model environmental adaptations of a TRP mode model is provided. A plurality of models are stored at the terminal device 110. Terminal device 110 sends information of the TRP index of its pre-stored TRP pattern model and its received channel measurements to network device 140. Since the network device 140 has an inherent knowledge of all TRP locations and has stored the radio channel dataset of the entire area, the network device 140 can use the above information from the terminal device 110 to evaluate which TRP mode model is most suitable for the current radio environment of the terminal device 110. In process 200, the network device 140 provides information about a target TRP mode model that is the most appropriate positioning model for the current wireless environment, that is, the adaptability between the model and the wireless environment is monitored. By monitoring the adaptability between the model and the wireless environment, consistency between training and reasoning about additional conditions on the NW side can be ensured, thereby improving AI/ML positioning accuracy.

Hereinafter, an exemplary signaling process 300 for monitoring a TRP pattern model according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 3. It is to be appreciated that UE 310 in fig. 3 may be an example of terminal device 110 in fig. 1 and 2, and LMF 340 in fig. 3 may be an example of network device 140 in fig. 2 and 1.

At S1, which shows a precondition, the UE 310 may pre-store several fixed TRP pattern models related to the located region and select one model for location from the several fixed TRP pattern models. It should be noted that the pre-stored TRP patterns of the fixed TRP pattern models may not overlap each other. For example, TRP 0,1,2,3 is stored for the first fixed TRP pattern model (e.g., TRP 0,1,2,3 is selected for training the first fixed TRP pattern model). TRP 0,1,2, 4 is stored for the second fixed TRP pattern model, e.g. for training the second fixed TRP pattern model, TRP 0, 2,3, 4 is stored for the third fixed TRP pattern model, e.g. for training the third fixed TRP pattern model.

At S2, the UE 310 may request the LMF 340 to monitor the adaptability between the selected fixed TRP mode model and the wireless environment by transmitting a request message. Since UE 310 has little knowledge of TRP deployment information and the local wireless environment (e.g., deployment of TRPs 120 and 130), UE 310 is unaware of model environment adaptation. However, the LMF 340 has global knowledge of the wireless environment and TRP location information, such as location information of all TRPs for the entire region. Thus, the UE 310 may request the LMF to monitor the adaptability between the selected fixed TRP mode model and the wireless environment. That is, when the UE 310 stores several fixed TRP mode models and wants to determine whether the currently selected model is the most appropriate model, the UE 310 may send a request for model context adaptation monitoring to the LMF 340.

At S3, upon receiving the monitoring request, the LMF 340 may query the UE 310 for necessary information for monitoring. That is, when the LMF 340 receives the request, the LMF 340 may query the UE 310 for necessary information. In some embodiments, the necessary information includes an input TRP index for each pre-stored model and received channel measurements of the UE, such as CIR or PDP, etc. At S4, the UE 310 provides necessary information to the LMF 340.

At S5, using the received information and a pre-stored data set in the LMF 340 or a data set downloaded from a data center, the LMF 340 may determine information on a most appropriate fixed TRP mode model for positioning at the current wireless environment of the UE based on a fixed TRP mode model selection mechanism, which will be described with reference to fig. 4. At S6, based on the result of the determination, the LMF 340 may transmit information about an appropriate fixed TRP mode model for positioning to the UE 310. In some embodiments, the information about the predicted or determined suitable model may include the TRP pattern of the model.

In some embodiments, LMF 340 may determine whether UE 310 needs to switch the current model based on information about the predicted fixed TRP mode model, and then send an indication of the model and the above information to UE 310, e.g., the TRP mode of the predicted fixed TRP mode model. That is, the LMF 340 may determine whether the UE 310 should switch the fixed TRP mode model based on a predicted cluster index indicating an appropriate positioning model for the UE 310. If the indicated model is different from the model currently used by the UE 310, it indicates that the model used by the UE 310 is not suitable for its current environment, and the LMF 340 may determine that the UE 310 should switch to the indicated model, and the LMF 340 may send the TRP mode of the indicated and indicated model to the UE 310. If the indicated model is the same as the model currently used by the UE 310, it indicates that the model used by the UE 310 is appropriate for its current environment, and the LMF 340 may determine that the UE 310 may not switch to the current model, and the LMF 340 may send information to the UE 310 indicating and the indicated model (which is also the current model).

In some embodiments, upon receiving information about the predicted fixed TRP mode model, the UE 310 may determine whether the predicted fixed TRP mode model is the same as the current model, if so, the UE 310 may not switch the current model, and if not, the UE 310 may switch from the current model to the predicted model.

Hereinafter, an exemplary flowchart 400 of a model selection process according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 4, and an exemplary illustration of TRP locations and TRP patterns of a model according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 5.

As shown in fig. 5, the data set (e.g., data of gray points) may be pre-ordered in the LMF 340, and the data set may represent the location coordinate tags for the TRPs of the entire region and the channel measurements of those TRPs. That is, the LMF 340 has TRP deployment knowledge and wireless channel information of the entire region.

As shown in fig. 5, the UE 310 may store three fixed TRP pattern models with different TRP patterns. The first fixed TRP pattern model is represented by a black circle and the TRP patterns of the first fixed TRP pattern model include TRP 1-1、TRP1-2、TRP1-3 and TRP 1-4. As shown in fig. 5, the second fixed TRP pattern model is represented by a black triangle, and the TRP patterns of the second fixed TRP pattern model include TRP 2-1、TRP2-2、TRP2-3 and TRP 2-4. As shown in fig. 5, the third fixed TRP pattern model is represented by a black rectangle, and the TRP patterns of the third fixed TRP pattern model including TRP 3-1、TRP3-2、TRP3-3 and TRP3-4.TRP1-1、TRP1-2、TRP1-3、TRP1-4、TRP2-1、TRP2-2、TRP2-3、TRP2-4、TRP3-1、TRP3-2、TRP3-3 and TRP 3-4 may be some specific points selected from gray points, and LMF 340 possesses TRP deployment knowledge and radio channel information of these TRPs upon receiving an input TRP index from UE 310.

As shown in fig. 5, for the TRP pattern of each model, all coordinates of the TRP used in each model form a convex polygon in the map, e.g., TRP 1-1、TRP1-2、TRP1-3 and TRP 1-4 form a polygon with a center C1 represented by a black star for the first fixed TRP pattern model, and TRP 2-1、TRP2-2、TRP2-3 and TRP 2-4 form a polygon with a center C2 represented by a black star for the second fixed TRP pattern model. For the third fixed TRP pattern model, TRP 3-1、TRP3-2、TRP3-3 and TRP 3-4 form polygons with center C3 represented by a black star.

When the LMF 340 receives information about the UE input TRP index of each pre-stored model and the received channel measurements of the UE, the LMF 340 will select the most appropriate model based on a fixed TRP mode model selection mechanism and determine whether the UE should switch models.

As shown in fig. 4, at 410, LMF 340 may calculate a positional center (e.g., center C1, center C2, or center C3) of a polygon (e.g., convex polygon) formed from coordinates of TRP used in each model. In some embodiments, the center of the polygon may be the geometric center of the polygon, the center of the least squares fit, the center of the minimum bounding rectangle. The center of the polygon (e.g., center C1, center C2, or center C3) may be recorded as a "location coordinate cluster center". Alternatively, the center may serve as an initial point for a subsequent iterative cluster computation of the converging cluster center. That is, locating the coordinate cluster center may serve as an initial point for subsequent iterative cluster computation to achieve a converging cluster center.

For example, LMF 340 receives three potentially fixed TRP mode models from UE 310. As shown in fig. 5, LMF 340 may form a convex polygon for each TRP pattern model of each model on a map using a particular TRP index and TRP coordinates used in each model. LMF 340 treats the location coordinate center (e.g., center C1, center C2, or center C3) of each model as a location coordinate cluster center.

The LMF 340 has a pre-stored dataset consisting of channel measurements and ground truth localization coordinate tags for the entire area, such as the gray points shown in fig. 5. At 420, for each location center, LMF 140 may select samples from the pre-stored dataset of LMFs that have a closest distance to the "location center" of each TRP mode model as the channel measurement cluster center. For example, LMF 340 may select point S1 closest to center C1 for the first fixed TRP mode model, point S2 closest to center C2 for the second fixed TRP mode model, and point S3 closest to center C3 for the third fixed TRP mode model, as shown in fig. 5. LMF 340 may then record or store the channel measurements for the selected point S1, S2, or S3 as a "channel measurement cluster center".

At 430, using channel measurement cluster centers, e.g., channel measurements for samples S1, S2, and S3, LMF 340 uses a cluster algorithm (e.g., k-means cluster) to predict which cluster center the received UE channel measurement should belong to. As shown in fig. 5, the location of the UE 310 is represented by a black cross. As shown in fig. 5, using the channel measurements received from UE 310 and the channel measurements of samples S1, S2, and S3, LMF 340 may predict that cluster center S2 may be the target cluster center to which the UE channel measurements belong.

At 440, based on the target cluster center determined at 430, LMF 340 may determine a most appropriate positioning model for the current environment of UE 310. As shown in fig. 5, LMF 340 may determine that the second fixed TRP mode model may be an ideal model. That is, the prediction cluster center (e.g., S2) indicates an appropriate fixed TRP pattern model (e.g., a second fixed TRP pattern model) of the current location of the UE.

The LMF 340 will determine whether the UE 310 should switch to the fixed TRP mode model based on the predicted cluster center index indicating the appropriate positioning model for the UE. If the indicated model is different from the model currently used by the UE, it indicates that the model used by the UE is not suitable for its current environment and the UE should switch to the indicated model.
